items.prompt: Black has a pawn on c5 and a king on g8. White has a pawn on f3. Tap every square the white piece on e4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on e4 can move to.

hints: Go around the piece one direction at a time, eight in all.
One direction is closed by White's own pawn on f3. Which one?
Seven lines are open. The pawn on c5 is on none of them.
items.explain: The queen on e4 reaches 24 squares. Her own pawn on f3 closes the line down and to the right, so that line is empty. The pawn on c5 is a knight's jump away, and the queen does not jump.

items.prompt: Two white pawns stand next to the queen. Tap every square the white queen on e4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on e4 can move to.

hints: Count the lines. Two of them are closed by White's own pawns.
The line to the left and the line downward are closed straight away.
On two other lines there is a black pawn: she may land on it and stop.
items.explain: Her own pawns on d4 and e3 close two lines at once, so the queen cannot move left or down. Her other lines are open, and on two of them she can take a black pawn (b7 and g6) and must stop there.

items.prompt: Can the white queen on a1 take the black rook on a8 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn on a4 stands between the queen and the rook, so the queen cannot reach a8.
She can take the pawn, which is the first piece on the line.

hints: Look at the squares between the queen and the rook.
Is every square between a1 and a8 empty?
A black pawn stands on a4. The queen sees only as far as the first piece.
items.explain: The a-file holds a black pawn on a4, so the queen's line upward ends there: she can take that pawn, but not the rook behind it. A piece behind a blocker is not in her reach.

items.prompt: The white bishop stands on d3. Can the white queen on d1 go to d6 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop on d3 is in the way of the file.
She can still step up to d2, in front of her own bishop.

hints: Is the file from d1 to d6 clear?
Which piece stands on it?
A queen does not jump over her own pieces either.
items.explain: Her own bishop on d3 closes the line up the d-file. She can go as far as d2 and no further. Nothing jumps over pieces except the knight.

items.prompt: It is White's move. Is the white queen on d4 attacked by a black piece right now? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on e6 is a jump away, so the queen cannot take it back.

hints: Look for black pieces near the queen. How does each one move?
The knight on e6 is one file right and two ranks up from the queen's square.
A knight attacks by jumping, so it attacks the queen on d4 although she cannot attack it.
items.explain: The black knight on e6 attacks the queen on d4 with its jump. The queen cannot capture it, because e6 is not on any of her lines. Attacks are not always mutual: the cheaper piece can attack her and be safe.

items.prompt: White to move. The queen can take two black units. Which capture is the safe one?
hints: For each capture ask: what could Black take back?
The pawn on e5 is guarded by the pawn on d6.
The knight on a6 has no guard, so taking it costs nothing.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 is guarded by the pawn on d6, so taking it would lose the queen for a pawn. The knight on a6 is unguarded, so the queen takes it for free.

feedback_by_move.e2e5: The pawn on d6 takes the queen back: nine counting points lost for one.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the queen on b5 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on b5 can move to.

hints: Look at the white king first. Is it safe?
The black rook gives check along the e-file. A move must end the check.
Only a move that stands between the rook and the king, or takes the rook, is allowed.
items.explain: The white king is in check from the rook on e8, so the queen may only make the check stop: block on e5 or e2, or take the rook on e8. Her other lines are closed to her for this move.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the piece on d4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the piece on d4 can move to.

hints: Name the piece first, then trace its lines one by one.
Two lines end early: one at the pawn on f4, one in front of the king on g1.
The black pawn on c6 is on none of her lines.
items.explain: The piece is a queen. Her own pawn on f4 stops the line to the right after e4, and her own king on g1 stops the diagonal after f2. The pawn on c6 is a knight's jump away and is not reachable.

items.prompt: Black to move. One queen slide ends the game. Which move?
hints: Look at the White king and what surrounds it.
White's own pawns fill the squares in front of the king.
The d-file is open from d8 to d1.
items.explain: The queen slides down the open d-file to d1 and gives check along the first rank. The white king cannot step forward because its own pawns stand there, and nothing can block or take the queen.
